Minor: RefreshScheduler.swift:198 applies the minimum-delay floor again (max(UpdateChecker.minimumRetryDelay, delay)) on top of the floor inside the static delayUntilNextCheck. It is needed because the static function returns 0 when a check is due, but the floor rule now lives in two places. Low priority: consider having the instance delayUntilNextCheck() return the floored value.

Minor: update_loop_not_started_when_disabled (RefreshSchedulerTests.swift:368) proves absence with 5 Task.yield() calls, which is a weak negative proof. It is acceptable because the guard it tests is synchronous.

Check: startUpdateCheckLoop now reads updates.config.enabled once at start. If [updates] enabled can be flipped at runtime without rebuilding the scheduler, the loop will not start until relaunch. Confirm how config reload works.

docs/SDD-auto-update-checker.md:19,26-32,104 still describes the old rule: 'intervalo mínimo de 24h', no network request if under 24 h, and invariant 104 'Nunca disparar checagem ... com intervalo inferior a 24 horas'. The new calendar-day rule breaks that on purpose, since a check late on one day followed by one just after midnight is less than 24 h apart. The SDD is a design spec from the original feature PR (ef6f7d4), not one of the lockstep docs (README, CLAUDE/AGENTS, config example, Localizable.strings), so this is a follow-up and does not block this batch. Suggest a note in the SDD pointing to UPDATE-SCHED-001 so no one restores the 24 h floor from the spec.

LOW (out of scope): if [updates] owner_repo is invalid (empty or has no '/'), check() returns at UpdateChecker.swift:189 before recordCheckDate. lastCheckDate then never advances, so the check stays due (delay 0), the loop at RefreshScheduler.swift:198 wakes every 60 s (the floor) instead of once a day, and it resets status = .failed each time. There is no network traffic and the cost is trivial. Recording the attempt date, or backing off to the next day on a config error, would restore the daily cadence.
